reason: The new .next is SEC followed by an exact copy of next_c's body (DEC ds_c; BEQ done; BIT dm_flip; BPL step_forward; LDA b_ptr; SBC #8; STA b_ptr; BCC step_back_hi; JMP each), so every exit (done/RTS, step_forward, step_back_hi, each) sees the same A, X, Y, flags (C=1 from SEC, which DEC and BIT leave alone; N/Z/V from the same DEC and BIT) and memory as when it went through BRA next_c. The only ways in to .next are JMP next at render.6502 1670 (to_next, from empty and clip_test's BCC) and 1690. Nothing else in src/ names next/next_c, and there is no label+N or table reference. next_c still falls through from part_byte unchanged. No stack use, no extra memory access, and nothing the IRQ can see differently. Listing addresses: .next is &9CA1. In the new layout BEQ done (->&9CD9), BPL step_forward (->&9CB5) and BCC step_back_hi (->&9CCB) all stay inside page &9C, so they get no page-cross penalty. Saves the 3-cycle BRA per execution. Bytes: +19 inline, -2 for the BRA, net +17 (the claim's -17 is that cost, shown with a minus sign). The page crossings downstream in bank 4 are the machine lens's job, and the candidate's measurement includes them.
